correctness.rationale: With C=B^{-1}, a positive fixed point obeys CHC=H-H^2. The right side is positive semidefinite and has the same rank as H, excluding eigenvalue 1; its range is then ran(H). The left side has range C ran(H), so C preserves the support and its orthogonal complement. On the support, H^(1/2) C H^(1/2) is the unique positive square root of H^2(I-H), so C=(I-H)^(1/2) there. This gives exactly the projector classification and its Grassmannian components, and substitution proves sufficiency. The differentiated map on a joint eigenbasis is diagonal on the real Hermitian matrix-unit basis: one real direction per diagonal entry and two per off-diagonal pair. With selected and omitted gains all in (1,3), the omitted block contributes m^2 expanding dimensions, mixed pairs have multiplier sqrt(a_omitted/a_selected), and selected-selected multipliers (a+b-ab)/sqrt(ab) decrease in either gain from the limiting value +1 at (1,1) to -1 at (3,3). Simplicity excludes a mixed unit multiplier. For the general candidate sink, omitted gains below 1 are strictly contracting in both omitted-omitted and mixed modes, including repeated gains. Omitting any gain above 1 gives an expanding diagonal mode; gain 1 forces +1, and gain at least 3 gives either an omitted expanding mode or an active multiplier at most -1. This proves the full local, hyperbolic criterion, not global convergence or stability at neutral gains. The extra bound B^2<=4I is only needed for invariance of the interval.
residual_risks: Finite rational witnesses in the supplied verifier do not certify the all-size theorem; the support argument and complete derivative eigensystem supply the proof.

value.rationale: Although the dynamics allows states that do not commute with B, every positive equilibrium commutes with B, and the theorem classifies them even on rank-deficient supports. Counting all real modes gives information invisible to the scalar or diagonal model: for two ordered gains in (1,3), selecting only the smaller gain gives index 3, while selecting only the larger gives index 1. The classification and exact local criterion thus resolve a natural stability question, without extrapolating to basins or chaotic dynamics.
residual_risks: The index formula applies to simple squared gains in (1,3), and the sink test does not decide nonlinear stability at neutral gains.
